# Elm Quay trial gives shifts one view of repairs

Elm Quay Housing's maintenance team spent eight weeks testing a shared repair log from Svale Systems in two buildings. Operations managers planning something similar can see what the preparation took, what an internal note shows and leaves open, and why the maintenance supervisor would run the trial again with one change.

By Thomas Barregren

At Elm Quay Housing, which manages 640 flats, telephone reports and emails used to be stored separately. In September 2025, the company's own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. How that went is recorded in an internal trial note and described by Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, Maya Lind.

## Why Elm Quay wanted one log

The team chose Svale Systems to supply the log after testing whether it could show the status of each repair. Answering questions by email, Lind describes the starting point:

> “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

## What the setup demanded

Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The team also kept telephone reporting open for residents.

Lind points to where the preparation time went:

> “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

## The trial note stops short of crediting the software

The trial ran for eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal note on it, dated December 4, 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered; emergencies and work ordered before the trial are excluded.

Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial, compared with three in the preceding eight weeks. The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.

These figures concern assignment, not completion. There are no measurements of cost, resident satisfaction, or completion time.

## Maya Lind looks back on the trial

Lind stopped short of recommending Svale to every housing company. Of the trial itself, she writes:

> “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

## Any expansion waits on larger repairs

The trial has not yet been expanded. Before deciding whether to expand it, the team will check how its categories work for larger repairs.

Operations managers weighing a similar trial can start by reading the [implementation checklist](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).

# Elm Quay trial gives shifts one view of repairs

Elm Quay Housing's maintenance team spent eight weeks testing a shared repair log from Svale Systems in two buildings. Operations managers planning something similar can see what the preparation took, what an internal note shows and leaves open, and why the maintenance supervisor would run the trial again with one change.

By Thomas Barregren

At Elm Quay Housing, which manages 640 flats, telephone reports and emails used to be stored separately. In September 2025, the company's own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings. How that went is recorded in an internal trial note and described by Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, Maya Lind.

## Why Elm Quay wanted one log

The team chose Svale Systems to supply the log after testing whether it could show the status of each repair. Answering questions by email, Lind describes the starting point:

> “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”

## What the setup demanded

Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The team also kept telephone reporting open for residents.

Lind points to where the preparation time went:

> “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

## The trial note stops short of crediting the software

The trial ran for eight weeks. Elm Quay's internal note on it, dated December 4, 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered; emergencies and work ordered before the trial are excluded.

Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial, compared with three in the preceding eight weeks. The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.

These figures concern assignment, not completion. There are no measurements of cost, resident satisfaction, or completion time.

## Maya Lind looks back on the trial

Lind stopped short of recommending Svale to every housing company. Of the trial itself, she writes:

> “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

## Any expansion waits on larger repairs

The trial has not yet been expanded. Before deciding whether to expand it, the team will check how its categories work for larger repairs.

Operations managers weighing a similar trial can start by reading the [implementation checklist](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist).

# Source-support report: prose-2.md

Draft: prose-2.md (en_US). Source: source.md (English). The quotations are English, so none were translated and no translation findings apply. The byline "Thomas Barregren" comes from the invocation and is not a finding.

## Claim accounting

| # | Draft passage | Source passage | Difference / test | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T | Title: "Elm Quay trial gives shifts one repair view" | "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." / Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us" / "The trial lasted eight weeks." / "in two buildings" | The material gives shift-sharing as the team's **aim**. Lind says one view "helps us" but does not say that shifts in fact share it. The title states the outcome for shifts as achieved, in the present tense and without the two-building scope. See Finding 1. | Finding 1 |
| S1 | "Elm Quay Housing's maintenance team spent eight weeks testing a shared repair log from Svale Systems in two buildings." | "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings" / "It chose Svale Systems" / "The trial lasted eight weeks." | Same subject, thing, scope and duration. | Supported |
| S2 | "Operations managers planning something similar can see what the preparation took, what an internal note shows and leaves open," | "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions"; Lind: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports."; note figures; "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements." | This is a preview of the article's content, and the article delivers it. | Supported |
| S3 | "and why maintenance supervisor Maya Lind would run the trial again with more time for preparation." | Lind: "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation." | "more time" is a broader form of "an extra week" and does not contradict it. "why" rests on her own adjacent reason ("helps us"). Her conditional modality ("would") is kept. | Supported |
| B | "By Thomas Barregren" | none (invocation) | Excluded by the task. | Not a finding |
| 1a | "At Elm Quay Housing, which manages 640 flats, telephone reports and emails used to be stored separately." | "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats." / "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately." | Same. | Supported |
| 1b | "In September 2025, the company's own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings." | "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings." | Same. "the company's" and the source's "its" both refer to Elm Quay Housing (third person singular, no natural gender). | Supported |
| 1c | "How that went is recorded in an internal trial note and described by Elm Quay maintenance supervisor Maya Lind." | "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says…" / "Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind" | Lind is identified as the customer's supervisor, which is supported. | Supported |
| H1 | Heading: "Why Elm Quay wanted one log" | "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." / "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately." | The heading uses "Elm Quay" for its maintenance team. Body 1b names the team explicitly, and the company remains the acting party. This is a customary metonymy, and the reason given is the sourced one. | Supported |
| 2a | "The team chose Svale Systems to supply the log after testing whether it could show the status of each repair." | "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available." | Same. "it" refers to the log (third person singular, neuter). The draft claims no comparison with other suppliers. | Supported |
| 2b | "Answering questions by email, Lind describes the starting point:" | "All interviews occurred by email" | Supported. The present tense is narrative present. | Supported |
| Q1 | "We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log." | Identical in the source list. | Verbatim. "We/us/ours" is first person plural, the speaker's team, as in the source. | Supported |
| 3a | "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions." | Identical sentence. | Same. Supplier narration is in third person. | Supported |
| 3b | "The team also kept telephone reporting open for residents." | "The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents." | Same subject and act. The category design is conveyed by Q1. | Supported |
| 3c | "Lind describes the setup from the team's side:" | Q2 (below) | This is a framing that the quotation bears out. | Supported |
| Q2 | "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts." | Identical. | Verbatim. | Supported |
| H2 | Heading: "The note does not credit the software for quicker assignment" | "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period. … the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." | "quicker assignment" describes the lower median observed, and the heading attributes no cause. "does not credit" matches "does not attribute". | Supported |
| 4a | "The trial ran for eight weeks." | "The trial lasted eight weeks." | Same. | Supported |
| 4b | "Elm Quay's internal note on it, dated December 4, 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered; emergencies and work ordered before the trial are excluded." | "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial." | Same. The exclusion attaches to the note's count, and the date format is localized. | Supported |
| 4c | "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial, compared with three in the preceding eight weeks." | "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period." | Same measure (assignment, median, working days) and the same periods. | Supported |
| 4d | "The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software." | Identical in substance. | Same. The disclaimer is attributed to the note, as in the source. | Supported |
| 4e | "These figures concern assignment, not completion." | "Median time from report to assignment…" / "There are no … completion-time measurements." / Forbidden: "Do not turn assignment time into completion time." | This is the author's clarification and rests on supported material. | Supported |
| 4f | "There are no measurements of cost, resident satisfaction, or completion time." | "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements." | Same. | Supported |
| H3 | Heading: "Maya Lind looks back on the trial" | Q3 | Framing only. | Supported |
| 5a | "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company." | Identical sentence. | Verbatim. The source's own scope ambiguity is carried over unchanged, and the customer's reservation survives. | Supported |
| 5b | "Of the trial itself, she writes:" | "All interviews occurred by email"; "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." | "she" is third person singular with female natural gender. The source's own "Her" establishes the natural gender. "writes" fits the email interview. | Supported |
| Q3 | "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation." | Identical. | Verbatim. The qualification ("but … extra week") is kept. | Supported |
| H4 | Heading: "Any expansion waits on larger repairs" | "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | This compresses "waits on [how the categories work for] larger repairs". "wait on" means "depend on", which holds whether or not the larger repairs have already occurred. I could name no case in which the source holds and the heading fails. | Supported |
| 6a | "The trial has not yet been expanded." | "The trial has not yet expanded" | Same. | Supported |
| 6b | "Before deciding whether to expand it, the team will check how its categories work for larger repairs." | "the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs." | The object of "decide" is expansion, which the preceding clause settles. "its" refers to the team (third person singular, no natural gender), and the categories are the team's ("designed its categories"; "The categories were ours"). | Supported |
| 7 | "Operations managers weighing a similar trial can start by reading the [implementation checklist](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist)." | Brief: "The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial." | The link text and verb ("reading") describe the destination accurately. The next step is optional ("can"), as the brief says. | Supported |

### Pronoun accounting (person, number, natural gender)
- "the company's" / "its" (source) → Elm Quay Housing: third person singular, no natural gender.
- "it" (2a) → the log: third person singular, neuter.
- "she" (5b) → Maya Lind: third person singular. The female natural gender rests on the source's "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment."
- "its" (6b) → the maintenance team: third person singular, collective, no natural gender.
- "it" (6b, "expand it") → the trial: third person singular, neuter.
- "We / us / ours / I" (quotations) → the speaker's team and Lind herself. These are verbatim and match the source.
- "that" (1c, "How that went") → the trial decision and trial. No person or gender features.

No pronoun adds or changes person, number or natural-gender information.

## Findings

### Finding 1: Source support, title (PLAUSIBLE)
- **Draft:** "Elm Quay trial gives shifts one repair view"
- **Source:** "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." / Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us" / "The trial lasted eight weeks." / "in two buildings".
- **What differs:** The source gives shift-sharing as the team's aim ("wanted"). Lind's assessment is that "one view of the reports helps us". It does not say the trial achieved shared visibility across shifts. The title turns the aim into an achieved outcome for "shifts", in the timeless present, and leaves out the two-building scope.
- **Case (title holds, source fails / source holds, title fails):** Suppose the log gave the team one view that helped it, but some staff on the evening shift were not among the six trained and did not consult the log. Lind's statement and every supplied fact remain true, and the title's claim that the trial gives shifts one view fails. No supplied statement excludes this case. It rests on the material staying silent about whether the aim was met. Because Lind's "one view … helps us" can naturally be read to cover the team's shifts, the finding is marked PLAUSIBLE rather than CONFIRMED.
- **Smallest supported repair:** Keep the aim as an aim, or use Lind's own terms. For example: "Elm Quay tests one repair log for its shifts", or "Elm Quay trial: one view of repair reports 'helps us'".

## Translation findings
None. The source and the draft are both in English, and all three quotations appear verbatim.

## Completion status
The comparison is complete. All claims in the title, summary, headings, body, quotations and link were accounted for. One unresolved finding remains: Finding 1 (title turns the shift-sharing aim into an achieved outcome; PLAUSIBLE). There are no translation findings.

# Source-support report: prose-1.md

Draft language: American English (en_US). Source language: English. No quotations are translated, so there are no translation findings. The byline "Thomas Barregren" comes from the invocation and is not assessed.

## Claim accounting

Each item gives the draft passage (D), the source passage (S) and the result. "Supported" means I could name no case compatible with the material in which one statement holds and the other fails.

### Title

1. D: "Elm Quay trial gives shifts one repair view"
   S: "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." / "shared repair log" / Lind: "Having one view of the reports helps us"
   Difference: the draft states as an outcome what the team set out to do. Lind's quotation presupposes that a single view exists and that it serves "us" (the team, which works in shifts), and the log is a "shared" one. Scope (two buildings) is carried by "trial". "Repair view" and "view of the reports" name the same thing here. Supported. Case tested: a single view exists but the shifts cannot use it. "shared repair log" together with "one view of the reports helps us" excludes this.

### Standfirst

2. D: "Elm Quay Housing's maintenance team spent eight weeks testing a shared repair log from Svale Systems in two buildings."
   S: "its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings" / "It chose Svale Systems" / "The trial lasted eight weeks."
   Supported.

3. D: "Operations managers planning something similar can see what the preparation took, what an internal note shows and leaves open,"
   S: the configuration, training and category material; the trial note; "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements."
   This is the author's framing of supported content. Supported. (The "preparation" label is discussed under item 13.)

4. D: "and why the maintenance supervisor would run the trial again with one change."
   S: "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation." / "Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"
   - "why ... would run the trial again": Lind's next sentence ("Having one view of the reports helps us") gives the reason in her own words. Supported.
   - "with one change": FINDING F2.
   - "the maintenance supervisor": FINDING F4.

### Opening

5. D: "At Elm Quay Housing, which manages 640 flats, telephone reports and emails used to be stored separately."
   S: "Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats." / "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately."
   "Used to be" carries the same time reference as "Previously", and it is equally vague about scope. Supported.

6. D: "In September 2025, the company's own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings."
   S: "In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings."
   Supported, nearly verbatim. "Its" is neuter and refers to the company; the draft makes that referent explicit.

7. D: "How that went is recorded in an internal trial note and described by Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, Maya Lind."
   S: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025" / "Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"
   The note and the interview are supported, and "customer interview" establishes that Lind is at Elm Quay. The appositive "Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, Maya Lind" is part of FINDING F4.

### "Why Elm Quay wanted one log"

8. Heading D: "Why Elm Quay wanted one log"
   S: "The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information." / "Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately."
   Naming the company for its maintenance team is ordinary metonymy, and the team is Elm Quay's own. Supported.

9. D: "The team chose Svale Systems to supply the log after testing whether it could show the status of each repair."
   S: "It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available."
   Supported. The draft claims no comparison with other suppliers and no result for the test.

10. D: "Answering questions by email, Lind describes the starting point:"
    S: "All interviews occurred by email"
    Supported.

11. Quotation D: "We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log."
    S: identical.
    Verbatim. The first-person plural "we/us/ours" is the speaker's own. Supported.

### "What the setup demanded"

12. D: "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions. The team also kept telephone reporting open for residents."
    S: "Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions." / "The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents."
    Supported. Supplier narration stays in the third person.

13. D: "Lind points to where the preparation time went:"
    S: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts."
    FINDING F3.

14. Quotation D: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts."
    S: identical. Verbatim. Supported.

### "The trial note stops short of crediting the software"

15. Heading D: "The trial note stops short of crediting the software"
    S: "the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
    FINDING F1.

16. D: "The trial ran for eight weeks."
    S: "The trial lasted eight weeks." Supported.

17. D: "Elm Quay's internal note on it, dated December 4, 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered; emergencies and work ordered before the trial are excluded."
    S: "Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial."
    The date is reformatted for en_US only. The source is just as unclear as the draft about how far the exclusion reaches: "It" (the note) could cover the count or the whole note. The draft does not say the median figures include emergencies. Supported.

18. D: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial, compared with three in the preceding eight weeks."
    S: "Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period."
    Supported. The measure (median, report to assignment), the unit (working days) and both periods match.

19. D: "The two periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
    S: "The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
    Supported, nearly verbatim.

20. D: "These figures concern assignment, not completion. There are no measurements of cost, resident satisfaction, or completion time."
    S: "Median time from report to assignment" / "There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements."
    Supported. The first sentence is an authorial clarification that rests on the source's measure.

### "Maya Lind looks back on the trial"

21. Heading D: "Maya Lind looks back on the trial". Supported. It introduces her retrospective quotation.

22. D: "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company."
    S: "Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company." Verbatim. The reservation survives.

23. D: "Of the trial itself, she writes:"
    S: "Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment." / "All interviews occurred by email"
    Pronoun: "she" is third person singular and asserts natural feminine gender. The source's "Her", which refers to Lind, supports third person singular and feminine natural gender. "Writes" is supported by the email interview. The draft does not present the quotation as an inference from the figures, so it follows "It is not an inference from the figures." Supported.

24. Quotation D: "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation."
    S: identical. Verbatim, and the "but" qualification is kept. Supported.

### "Any expansion waits on larger repairs"

25. Heading D: "Any expansion waits on larger repairs"
    S: "The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs."
    This is a compressed heading, and the next sentence states the exact condition. No decision is made and no expansion occurs before the check, so "any expansion waits" holds. Defensible. Not a finding.

26. D: "The trial has not yet been expanded. Before deciding whether to expand it, the team will check how its categories work for larger repairs."
    S: as in item 25.
    Supported. "Its" is neuter and refers to the team, whose categories they are ("The maintenance team designed its categories").

27. D: "Operations managers weighing a similar trial can start by reading the [implementation checklist](https://example.invalid/svale/checklist)."
    S (brief): "The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial."
    The link text and verb describe the destination accurately. Supported.

### Checked and not findings

- No causal claim, no claim about savings or resident satisfaction, and no conversion of assignment time into completion time appears anywhere, including the title and headings.
- The brief says the case is supplier-published and not independent journalism. The draft makes no claim of independence. Whether to disclose this is an editorial matter outside this comparison.

## Findings (source support)

### F1. The heading widens what the note declines to credit (moderate)

- Draft: "The trial note stops short of crediting the software"
- Source: "the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software."
- Difference in scope and stance: the source limits the non-attribution to "the difference", meaning the change in median assignment time. The heading says the note does not credit the software at all. "Stops short" also suggests the note came close to crediting it, but the source says the note "explicitly" does not.
- Case: the note credits the software with making reports visible to both shifts, while it explicitly declines to attribute the shorter median to it. The source statement holds and the heading fails. No supplied statement rules this out, because the material reports only some of the note's content.
- Smallest repair: "The trial note does not credit the software with the difference"

### F2. "With one change" asserts that there was only one change (low)

- Draft (standfirst): "why the maintenance supervisor would run the trial again with one change."
- Source: "I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation."
- Difference in scope: Lind names one thing she would do differently. The draft says one change is all she would make.
- Case: Lind would repeat the trial with an extra preparation week and also with other changes she was not asked about. Her quotation holds and "with one change" fails. Nothing in the material says the extra week is her only change.
- Smallest repair: "...would run the trial again with more time for preparation."

### F3. "Where the preparation time went" goes beyond the comparison in the quotation (low)

- Draft: "Lind points to where the preparation time went:"
- Source: "We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts."
- Difference in the thing measured: Lind compares the time spent agreeing categories with the time spent entering the first reports. The lead-in presents the quotation as an account of how the preparation time was divided, which implies that categories took most of it. The material does not say how preparation time was split among category work, configuration and the two training sessions.
- Case: configuration and training took more of the preparation than category agreement, yet agreeing categories still took longer than entering the first reports. The quotation holds and the lead-in's implication fails. No supplied statement rules this out.
- Smallest repair: "Lind compares the work on categories with entering the first reports:"

### F4. The definite title makes Lind the only maintenance supervisor (low)

- Draft: "Elm Quay's maintenance supervisor, Maya Lind" (opening); "the maintenance supervisor" (standfirst)
- Source: "Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"
- Difference in number: the source gives Lind's role but not whether she is the only person in it. The possessive appositive and the definite standfirst present her as Elm Quay's sole maintenance supervisor.
- Case: Elm Quay, which manages 640 flats, has more than one maintenance supervisor. The source holds and the draft's wording fails. No supplied statement rules this out.
- Smallest repair: in the opening, "described by maintenance supervisor Maya Lind"; in the standfirst, "why maintenance supervisor Maya Lind would run the trial again..." (or "an Elm Quay maintenance supervisor").

## Translation findings

None. The source and the draft are both in English, and the three quotations match the source word for word.

## Completion status

Complete. All claims in the title, standfirst, headings, body, quotations and link were accounted for. Unresolved findings: F1 (moderate), F2, F3, F4 (low). No editorial questions remain open.
